summary: DeterminismContract also has a scalar no-execute validation gap: isSafeInteger() performs equality/modulo/absolute-value work without first proving the runtime value is a primitive number, and several exported functions reach it without their own type preflight. Malformed metatable-backed runtime arguments can therefore execute arithmetic/comparison metamethods while canonical deterministic input validation is trying to reject them. This is the same trust-boundary class already being closed elsewhere in Hero-Gate hardening and should be repaired together with the array/metatable finding, without changing accepted deterministic bytes or golden sequences.
evidence: main@aa7e04f05834ae783773c908fccfdbbe510558e5 isSafeInteger(value: number) evaluates value ~= value, value % 1, and math.abs(value) with no runtime type(value) == 'number' preflight.

hashParts(seed, parts), hex32(value), normalizeRngSeed(seed), nextRngState(state), and nextIntegerState(state, minimum, maximum) can reach assertU32()/isSafeInteger() without proving the runtime scalar type first.
seedFor(worldSeed, generationVersion, subsystemSalt, scopes) evaluates isSafeInteger(generationVersion) directly before any primitive-number runtime check.
tests/deterministic_rng.luau covers fractional/range-invalid numeric inputs but no hostile non-number scalar/metamethod cases; the accepted RNG/golden behavior need not change to close this boundary.

metadata.recommendedRegression: hostile scalar tables supplied as seed/state/minimum/maximum/generationVersion must reject with zero arithmetic/comparison metamethod executions; ordinary numeric golden outputs remain byte-for-byte unchanged
